opeds.headline: Without an Off-Switch, AI Progress Is Just Managed Collapse
opeds.subtitle: Unchecked artificial intelligence without enforceable human control is a civilizational hazard.
opeds.body:
We spent centuries building the institutional guardrails that keep society stable. On what authority do you claim we can remove them without inviting collapse? Complex human systems require boundaries to survive; removing those boundaries systematically triggers chaos.

Every high-consequence engineering discipline respects this constraint. The Boeing 737 MAX killed 346 people because the FAA delegated certification to the manufacturer, trading oversight for speed. When oversight vanishes, catastrophe follows not from malice, but from the unchecked momentum of uncorrected errors.

Human moral discernment cannot be reduced to computation or algorithmic optimization. The human heart represents a non-computable domain of historical memory and moral judgment that no synthetic architecture can replicate. Treating complex human agency as a mere technical bottleneck to be engineered away invites civilizational drift.

Technology companies deploy advanced models while treating safety mechanisms as optional patches rather than non-negotiable prerequisites. When algorithmic disgorgement forces the total destruction of illegally trained models, regulators acknowledge that tainted foundations cannot be salvaged by mere software updates. The architecture itself must be held accountable.

We must mandate dual kill criteria and absolute operational corrigibility across every deployment pipeline. Congress and federal regulators must enforce verifiable off-switches that grant named human actors the unassailable authority to halt autonomous systems. Ungoverned success is luck, not safety, and luck is a strategy that always runs out.
